title: Frontal cutaneous meningioma - Case report*
case_prompt:
A 55-year-old man presented with a slowly growing, asymptomatic tumoral lesion in the frontal region of the scalp, first noted 3 years earlier. He reported no pain, discharge, or overlying skin changes. His medical history was notable for significant head trauma 24 years earlier, resulting in a frontal bone fracture, right brachial plexus injury with resultant right arm palsy, encephalomalacia, and epilepsy managed with levetiracetam, oxazepam, and folic acid. He also had a remote subdural hematoma from a second head injury and a history of alcohol abuse.

On examination, there was a 2 × 3 cm firm, ovoid subcutaneous mass in the frontal area. The lesion was adherent to the underlying tissues but covered by normal-appearing skin. No cervical lymphadenopathy was palpable. 

A cranial computed tomography scan demonstrated a 2- to 3-cm soft-tissue mass in the frontal scalp, with an underlying bony defect in the frontal bone. There was evidence of encephalomalacia and ventricular asymmetry consistent with prior imaging, but no intracranial mass lesion was identified.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. The tumor’s meningothelial origin was supported by immunohistochemical positivity for EMA — “Immunohistochemical study showed that the cells were positive for EMA.”  
2. Mesenchymal differentiation consistent with meningioma was corroborated by vimentin positivity — “cells were positive for… vimentin.”  
3. An epithelial neoplasm was excluded by the absence of cytokeratin expression — “Staining for epithelial (cytokeratins)… was negative.”  
4. A melanocytic lesion was ruled out by negative S100 protein staining — “Staining for… S100 protein… was negative.”  
5. Vascular tumors such as hemangioma were excluded by lack of CD34 and CD31 expression — “Staining for vascular (CD34 and CD31)… was negative.”  
6. Histiocytic proliferations were negated by a negative CD68 stain — “Staining for… CD68… was negative.”  
7. Myogenic tumors were ruled out by absence of desmin and smooth muscle actin staining — “Staining for… desmin and smooth muscle actin… was negative.”
